commentary:
Energy is the morning's story: crude reversed Thursday's tightness-driven rally after reports the US and Iran are exploring a phased deal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting the blockade on Iranian ports. Brent slipped 1.1% to $105.44, WTI dropped 1.8% to $92.88 — with the WTI-Brent discount blowing out to its widest since early May near $12 — and the products led lower, gasoil off 5.2% and RBOB down 2.2%, while TTF and Henry Hub gas shed close to 4%. That cooling in oil eased the inflation panic that had driven global yields to multi-decade highs: Treasuries steadied, European bonds caught a bid, and equity index futures extended weekly gains, with the S&P up 0.3%, Nasdaq up 0.5% and Euro Stoxx banks outperforming at +1.5%.

The macro backdrop remains a hiking regime, not an easing one. The Fed's first hike in three years is being reinforced — Philadelphia's Paulson flagged further "modest" moves to tame inflation — while the BoE's Bailey says high energy costs make holding rates harder, and markets increasingly price two more UK hikes. The Trump-Xi summit delivered pomp but little substance beyond AI talks and hints at a trade truce extension, and Trump's stated concern about yen weakness lifted JPY 0.7%, the standout FX move. Gold (+1%) and silver (+2.1%) rallied despite the risk-on tone — a hedge against sticky inflation and heavy sovereign borrowing needs keeping real financing costs elevated.

In ags, grains sold off hard — CBOT wheat -2.2%, corn -1.8% — while arabica coffee added 1.3% near records amid the US-Colombia tariff back-and-forth, according to reports.
